{
    "layer": "top",
    "position": "top",
    "height": 34,
    "spacing": 4,

    "modules-left": ["clock"],
    "modules-center": ["hyprland/workspaces", "custom/workspace-tabs"],
    "modules-right": ["network", "bluetooth", "battery"],

    "hyprland/workspaces": {
        "format": "{name}",
	"all-outputs": true,
	"ignore-hidden": false,
        "on-click": "activate",
	"workspace-taskbar": true
    },

    "custom/workspace-tabs": {
	"exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/workspace-tabs.sh",
	"return-type": "json",
	"interval": "once",
	"signal": 8,
	"restart-interval": 0
    },

    "clock": {
        "format": "{:%H:%M}",
        "tooltip-format": "{:%A, %B %d, %Y}"
    },

    "network": {
	"interface": "wlo1",
	"format": "{ifname}",
	"format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%)  ",
	"format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"format-disconnected": "", //An empty format will hide the module.
	"format-disconnected": "",
	"tooltip-format": "{ifname}",
	"tooltip-format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%) ",
	"tooltip-format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"tooltip-format-disconnected": "Disconnected",
	"max-length": 50
    },

    "battery": {
        "format": "{capacity}% {icon}",
        "format-icons": ["[    ]", "[█   ]", "[██  ]", "[███ ]", "[████]"]
    },

    "bluetooth": {
	"format": " {status}",
	"format-disabled": "", // an empty format will hide the module
	"format-connected": " {num_connections}C",
	"tooltip-format": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}",
	"tooltip-format-connected": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}\n\n{device_enumerate}",
	"tooltip-format-enumerate-connected": "{device_alias}\t{device_address}"
    }
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	emit() {
5	  local ws
6	  ws=$(hyprctl -j activeworkspace | jq -r '.id')
7	
8	  local text
9	  text=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "$ws" '
10	    [ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) | .title ]
11	    | map(if length > 20 then .[:20] + "…" else . end)
12	    | join(" | ")
13	  ')
14	
15	  # Waybar expects a single JSON object per line
16	  jq -nc --arg t "$text" '{text: $t, tooltip: $t, class: "tabs"}'
17	}
18

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

emit() {
  local ws
  ws=$(hyprctl -j activeworkspace | jq -r '.id')

  local text
  text=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "$ws" '
    [ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) | .title ]
    | map(if length > 20 then .[:20] + "…" else . end)
    | join(" | ")
  ')

  # Waybar expects a single JSON object per line
  jq -nc --arg t "$text" '{text: $t, tooltip: $t, class: "tabs"}'
}

emit

# Subscribe to Hyprland events; re-emit on any window/workspace change
socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|renameworkspace*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

waybar-wlr-taskbar(5)         File Formats Manual        waybar-wlr-taskbar(5)

NAME
       waybar - wlr taskbar module

DESCRIPTION
       The  taskbar module displays the currently open applications. This mod‐
       ule requires a compositor that implements the  foreign-toplevel-manager
       interface.

CONFIGURATION
       Addressed by wlr/taskbar

       all-outputs:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If  set  to false applications on the waybar's current output will
       be shown. Otherwise, all applications are shown.

       format:
            typeof: string
            default: {icon}
            The format, how information should be displayed.

       icon-theme:
            typeof: array|string
            The names of the icon-themes that should be used to find an  icon.
       The  list  will be traversed from left to right. If omitted, the system
       default will be used.

       icon-size:
            typeof: integer
            default: 16
            The size of the icon.

       markup:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If set to true, pango  markup  will  be  accepted  in  format  and
       tooltip-format.

       tooltip:
            typeof: bool
            default: true
            If set to false no tooltip will be shown.

       tooltip-format:
            typeof: string
            default: {title}
            The format, how information in the tooltip should be displayed.

       active-first:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If  set  to  true, always reorder the tasks in the taskbar so that
       the currently active one is first. Otherwise don't reorder.

       sort-by-app-id:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If set to true, group tasks by their app_id. Cannot be  used  with
       'active-first'.

       on-click:
            typeof: string
            The action which should be triggered when clicking on the applica‐
       tion button with the left mouse button.

       on-click-middle:
            typeof: string
            The action which should be triggered when clicking on the applica‐
       tion button with the middle mouse button.

       on-click-right:
            typeof: string
            The action which should be triggered when clicking on the applica‐
       tion button with the right mouse button.

       on-update:
            typeof: string
            Command to execute when the module is updated.

       ignore-list:
            typeof: array
            List of app_id/titles to be invisible.

       app_ids-mapping:
            typeof: object
            Dictionary of app_id to be replaced with

       rewrite:
            typeof: object
            Rules to rewrite the module format output. See rewrite rules.

FORMAT REPLACEMENTS
       {icon}: The icon of the application.

       {name}:  The application name as in desktop file if appropriate desktop
       files are found, otherwise same as {app_id}

waybar-hyprland-workspaces(5) File Formats Manualwaybar-hyprland-workspaces(5)

NAME
       waybar - hyprland workspaces module

DESCRIPTION
       The  workspaces  module displays the currently used workspaces in hypr‐
       land compositor.

CONFIGURATION
       Addressed by hyprland/workspaces

       format:
            typeof: string
            default: {id}
            The format, how information should be displayed.

       format-icons:
            typeof: array
            Based on the workspace ID and state, the corresponding  icon  gets
       selected. See icons.

       window-rewrite:
            typeof: object
            Regex  rules to map window class to an icon or preferred method of
       representation for a workspace's window.
           Keys are the rules, while the values are the methods of representa‐
           tion. Values may use the placeholders {class} and  {title}  to  use
           the  window's  original  class and/or title respectively. Rules may
           specify `class<...>`, `title<...>`, or both in order  to  fine-tune
           the  matching.  You  may assign an empty value to a rule to have it
           ignored from generating any representation in workspaces.
           This setting is ignored if workspace-taskbar.enable is set to true.

       window-rewrite-default:
            typeof: string
            default: "?"
            The default method of representation  for  a  workspace's  window.
       This  will  be  used  for windows whose classes do not match any of the
       rules in window-rewrite.
            This setting is ignored  if  workspace-taskbar.enable  is  set  to
       true.

       format-window-separator:
            typeof: string
            default: " "
            The separator to be used between windows in a workspace.
            This  setting  is  ignored  if  workspace-taskbar.enable is set to
       true.

       workspace-taskbar:
            typeof: object
            Contains settings for the workspace taskbar, an  alternative  mode
       for the workspaces module which displays the window icons as images in‐
       stead of text.

               enable:
                    typeof: bool
                    default: false
                    Enables the workspace taskbar mode.

               format:
                    typeof: string
                    default: {icon}
                    Format  to  use  for each window in the workspace taskbar.
               Available placeholders are {icon} and {title}.

               icon-size:
                    typeof: int
                    default: 16
                    Size of the icons in the workspace taskbar.

               icon-theme:
                    typeof: string | array
                    default: []
                    Icon theme to use for the workspace taskbar. If  an  array
               is  provided,  the  first  theme that is found for a given icon
               will be used. If no theme is found (or the array is empty), the
               default icon theme is used.

               orientation:
                    typeof: "horizontal" | "vertical"
                    default: horizontal
                    Direction in which the workspace taskbar is displayed.

       show-special:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If set to true, special workspaces will be shown.

       special-visible-only:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If this and show-special are to true, special workspaces  will  be
       shown only if visible.

       persistent-only:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If set to true, only persistent workspaces will be shown on bar.

       all-outputs:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If  set  to  false workspaces group will be shown only in assigned
       output. Otherwise, all workspace groups are shown.

       active-only:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If set to true, only the active workspace will be shown.

       move-to-monitor:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If set to true, open the workspace on  the  current  monitor  when
       clicking on a workspace button.
           Otherwise, the workspace will open on the monitor where it was pre‐
           viously  assigned. Analog to using `focusworkspaceoncurrentmonitor`
           dispatcher instead of `workspace` in Hyprland.

       ignore-workspaces:
            typeof: array
            default: []
            Regexes to match against workspaces names. If there's a match, the
       workspace will not be shown. This takes precedence  over  show-special,
       all-outputs, and active-only.

       sort-by:
            typeof: string
            default: "default"
            If set to number, workspaces will sort by number.
           If  set  to name, workspaces will sort by name. If set to id, work‐
           spaces will sort by id. If set to special-centered, workspaces will
           sort by default with special workspaces in the center. If  none  of
           those, workspaces will sort with default behavior.

       expand:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            Enables this module to consume all left over space dynamically.

FORMAT REPLACEMENTS
       {id}: id of workspace assigned by compositor

       {name}: workspace name assigned by compositor

       {icon}: Icon, as defined in format-icons.

ICONS
       Additional  to  workspace name matching, the following format-icons can
       be set.

       •   default: Will be shown, when no string match is found and  none  of
           the below conditions have defined icons.
       •   active: Will be shown, when workspace is active
       •   special: Will be shown on non-active special workspaces
       •   empty:  Will  be  shown on non-active, non-special empty persistent
           workspaces
       •   visible: Will be shown on workspaces that are visible but  not  ac‐
           tive.  For  example:  this is useful if you want your visible work‐
           spaces on other monitors to have the same look as active.
       •   persistent: Will be shown on non-empty persistent workspaces

EXAMPLES
           "hyprland/workspaces": {
                "format": "{name}: {icon}",
                "format-icons": {
                     "1": "",
                     "2": "",
                     "3": "",
                     "4": "",
                     "5": "",
                     "active": "",
                     "default": ""
                },
                "persistent-workspaces": {
                     "*": 5, // 5 workspaces by default on every monitor
                     "HDMI-A-1": 3 // but only three on HDMI-A-1
                }
           }

           "hyprland/workspaces": {
                "format": "{name}: {icon}",
                "format-icons": {
                     "1": "",
                     "2": "",
                     "3": "",
                     "4": "",
                     "5": "",
                     "active": "",
                     "default": ""
                },
                "persistent-workspaces": {
                     "*": [ 2,3,4,5 ], // 2-5 on every monitor
                     "HDMI-A-1": [ 1 ] // but only workspace 1 on HDMI-A-1
                }
           }

           "hyprland/workspaces": {
                "format": "{name}n{windows}",
                "format-window-separator": "n",
                "window-rewrite-default": "",
                "window-rewrite": {
                     "title<.*youtube.*>": "", // Windows whose titles contain "youtube"
                     "class<firefox>": "", // Windows whose classes are "firefox"
                     "class<firefox> title<.*github.*>": "", // Windows whose class is "firefox" and title contains "github". Note that "class" always comes first.
                     "foot": "", // Windows that contain "foot" in either class or title. For optimization reasons, it will only match against a title if at least one other window explicitly matches against a title.
                     "code": "󰨞",
                     "title<.* - (.*) - VSCodium>": "codium $1"  // captures part of the window title and formats it into output
                }
           }

           "hyprland/workspaces": {
                // Formatting omitted for brevity
                "ignore-workspaces": [
                     "(special:)?chrome-sharing-indicator"
                ]
           }

Style
       •   #workspaces
       •   #workspaces button
       •   #workspaces button.active
       •   #workspaces button.empty
       •   #workspaces button.visible
       •   #workspaces button.persistent
       •   #workspaces button.special
       •   #workspaces button.urgent
       •   #workspaces button.hosting-monitor (gets applied if workspace-moni‐
           tor == waybar-monitor)
       •   #workspaces .taskbar-window (each window in the taskbar)

                                  2025-08-08     waybar-hyprland-workspaces(5)

lastPrompt: Build a taskbar in my waybar that is beside of my workspace tab and displays all the current tabs in the current workspace as their logos.

aiTitle: Add taskbar to waybar with workspace tabs

content.text: This confirms the diagnosis: someone tried to enable Hyprland's native `workspace-taskbar` mode (real icon images per window) but set it as a bare boolean instead of the required object schema, so it silently did nothing — and a fragile custom `socat`-based script showing plain text titles was bolted on as a workaround instead. I'll switch to the native mechanism, which gives actual app-icon images beside the workspace pills. Let me check file ownership/permissions and current icon theme first.

input.command:
whoami; id
echo "--- ownership ---"
ls -la ~/.config/waybar/config.jsonc ~/.config/waybar/style.css ~/.config/waybar/scripts/workspace-tabs.sh
echo "--- writable? ---"
[ -w ~/.config/waybar/config.jsonc ] && echo "config.jsonc writable" || echo "config.jsonc NOT writable"
echo "--- icon theme ---"
gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface icon-theme 2>/dev/null
cat ~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini 2>/dev/null | grep -i icon
echo "--- hypr autostart refs to workspace-tabs / waybar ---"
grep -rn "workspace-tabs\|waybar" ~/.config/hypr/*.conf 2>/dev/null
echo "--- screenshot tool ---"
which grim slurp hyprshot 2>/dev/null

**Facts:**
1. Files referencing `config.jsonc` / `workspace-tabs.sh`: only `config.jsonc` itself (self-reference to its own path in a comment/exec string). No Hyprland exec-once entries, no systemd units, nothing else imports or loads these files by path — waybar just reads `config.jsonc`/`style.css` from its default config dir at startup.
2. No functions/classes involved — these are runtime JSONC/CSS config files and a standalone shell script, not code with an API surface.
3. Not a data file — `config.jsonc` is waybar module configuration (module names, format strings, booleans/ints); no records/fields/dates to show.
4. User's instruction verbatim: "ran the chown, go ahead" — confirming ownership fix so I proceed with "editing config.jsonc, style.css, and workspace-tabs.sh to replace the broken custom/workspace-tabs text module with Hyprland's native workspace-taskbar icon mode (hyprland/workspaces#taskbar, active-only, workspace-taskbar.enable=true), add matching CSS, reload waybar ... and verify with a grim screenshot."

{
    "layer": "top",
    "position": "top",
    "height": 34,
    "modules-center": ["hyprland/workspaces", "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar"],
    "hyprland/workspaces": {
        "format": "{name}",
        "all-outputs": true,
        "on-click": "activate"
    },

        "format": "{windows}",

}
EOF

content.content:
{
    "layer": "top",
    "position": "top",
    "height": 34,
    "spacing": 4,

    "modules-left": ["clock"],
    "modules-center": ["hyprland/workspaces", "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar"],
    "modules-right": ["network", "bluetooth", "battery"],

    "hyprland/workspaces": {
        "format": "{name}",
	"all-outputs": true,
	"ignore-hidden": false,
        "on-click": "activate"
    },

    "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar": {
	"format": "{windows}",
	"all-outputs": false,
	"active-only": true,
	"on-click": "activate",
	"workspace-taskbar": {
	    "enable": true,
	    "format": "{icon}",
	    "icon-size": 20,
	    "icon-theme": ["Papirus"],
	    "orientation": "horizontal"
	}
    },

    "clock": {
        "format": "{:%H:%M}",
        "tooltip-format": "{:%A, %B %d, %Y}"
    },

    "network": {
	"interface": "wlo1",
	"format": "{ifname}",
	"format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%)  ",
	"format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"format-disconnected": "", //An empty format will hide the module.
	"format-disconnected": "",
	"tooltip-format": "{ifname}",
	"tooltip-format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%) ",
	"tooltip-format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"tooltip-format-disconnected": "Disconnected",
	"max-length": 50
    },

    "battery": {
        "format": "{capacity}% {icon}",
        "format-icons": ["[    ]", "[█   ]", "[██  ]", "[███ ]", "[████]"]
    },

    "bluetooth": {
	"format": " {status}",
	"format-disabled": "", // an empty format will hide the module
	"format-connected": " {num_connections}C",
	"tooltip-format": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}",
	"tooltip-format-connected": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}\n\n{device_enumerate}",
	"tooltip-format-enumerate-connected": "{device_alias}\t{device_address}"
    }
}

aiTitle: Add taskbar to waybar with workspace tabs

content.text:
It's live and working. Summary of what was going on and what I did:

**Root cause:** A previous attempt had already tried to build this exact feature via Hyprland's native `workspace-taskbar` mode, but it was set as a bare `"workspace-taskbar": true` instead of the required config object — so it silently did nothing. A fragile fallback (`custom/workspace-tabs.sh`, using `socat` to tail the Hyprland event socket and print plain window titles as text) was bolted on instead.

**Fix, in `~/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`:**
- Split `hyprland/workspaces` into two instances: the original (workspace-switcher pills) and a new `hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` beside it.
- Enabled the taskbar properly: `"workspace-taskbar": {"enable": true, "format": "{icon}", "icon-size": 20, "icon-theme": ["Papirus"]}`.
- The key fix that took the most digging: the outer `"format"` **must** contain the `{windows}` placeholder (undocumented in the man page's replacement list, only shown in an example) — without it, no per-window icons ever get inserted, regardless of the taskbar config.
- Set `"active-only": true` + `"all-outputs": false` so each monitor's taskbar shows only the windows on that monitor's currently active workspace (not every workspace, not other monitors).
- Added matching CSS (`#workspaces.taskbar .taskbar-window`) for spacing/hover — the module's CSS ID is shared (`#workspaces`) with an added `.taskbar` class, not a separate `#workspaces-taskbar` ID.
- Left the now-unused `workspace-tabs.sh` script in place per your call not to delete it.

Verified on both monitors: real app-icon images (Chrome, Ghostty, etc.) now render live, filtered strictly to the current workspace, right next to the workspace pills.

lastPrompt: There's an empty space on the right of the shown tabs on the taskbar. Additionally, please make some divider between the tabs and the workspace numbers.

aiTitle: Add taskbar to waybar with workspace tabs

content.text:
Confirmed on both monitors: divider is in place and no trailing empty space after the icons.

**What changed in `~/.config/waybar/style.css`:**
- `#workspaces.taskbar button:not(.active) { min-width: 0; padding: 0; margin: 0; border: none; }` — the empty placeholder buttons for non-active workspaces (which still got created due to `active-only` hiding their *content* but not the button itself) were reserving blank width; this collapses them to nothing.
- `#workspaces.taskbar { border-left: 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.15); margin-left: 6px; padding-left: 6px; }` — adds a subtle vertical divider line between the workspace numbers and the icon taskbar.

Both are live now (waybar reloaded, no errors) and verified on eDP-1 and HDMI-A-1.

aiTitle: Add taskbar to waybar with workspace tabs

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:?usage: workspace-tabs.sh <monitor-name>}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit

socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

emit() {
  local ws
  ws=$(hyprctl -j activeworkspace | jq -r '.id')

  local text
  text=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "$ws" '
    [ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) | .title ]
    | map(if length > 20 then .[:20] + "…" else . end)
    | join(" | ")
  ')

  # Waybar expects a single JSON object per line
  jq -nc --arg t "$text" '{text: $t, tooltip: $t, class: "tabs"}'
}

emit

# Subscribe to Hyprland events; re-emit on any window/workspace change
socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|renameworkspace*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

{
    "layer": "top",
    "position": "top",
    "height": 34,
    "spacing": 4,

    "modules-left": ["clock"],
    "modules-center": ["hyprland/workspaces", "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar"],
    "modules-right": ["network", "bluetooth", "battery"],

    "hyprland/workspaces": {
        "format": "{name}",
	"all-outputs": true,
	"ignore-hidden": false,
        "on-click": "activate"
    },

    "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar": {
	"format": "{windows}",
	"all-outputs": false,
	"active-only": true,
	"on-click": "activate",
	"workspace-taskbar": {
	    "enable": true,
	    "format": "{icon}",
	    "icon-size": 20,
	    "icon-theme": ["Papirus"],
	    "orientation": "horizontal"
	}
    },

    "clock": {
        "format": "{:%H:%M}",
        "tooltip-format": "{:%A, %B %d, %Y}"
    },

    "network": {
	"interface": "wlo1",
	"format": "{ifname}",
	"format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%)  ",
	"format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"format-disconnected": "", //An empty format will hide the module.
	"format-disconnected": "",
	"tooltip-format": "{ifname}",
	"tooltip-format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%) ",
	"tooltip-format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"tooltip-format-disconnected": "Disconnected",
	"max-length": 50
    },

    "battery": {
        "format": "{capacity}% {icon}",
        "format-icons": ["[    ]", "[█   ]", "[██  ]", "[███ ]", "[████]"]
    },

    "bluetooth": {
	"format": " {status}",
	"format-disabled": "", // an empty format will hide the module
	"format-connected": " {num_connections}C",
	"tooltip-format": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}",
	"tooltip-format-connected": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}\n\n{device_enumerate}",
	"tooltip-format-enumerate-connected": "{device_alias}\t{device_address}"
    }
}

RETURN-TYPE
       When  return-type  is  set  to json, Waybar expects the exec-script  to
       output its data in JSON format. This should look like this:

           {"text": "$text", "tooltip": "$tooltip", "class": "$class", "percentage": $percentage }

       The class parameter also accepts an array of strings.

=== general bar-level output ===
           them.

       output
            typeof: string|array
            Specifies  on which screen this bar will be displayed. Exclamation
       mark(!) can be used to exclude specific output.
           Output specification follows sway's and can either  be  the  output
           port  such as "HDMI-A-1" or a string consisting of the make, model,
           and serial such as "Some Company ABC123 0x00000000". See  sway-out‐
           put(5) for details. In an array, star '*' can be used at the end to
           accept all outputs, in case all previous entries are exclusions.

       position
            typeof: string
            default: top

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:?usage: workspace-tabs.sh <monitor-name>}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit

socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

{
    "layer": "top",
    "position": "top",
    "height": 34,
    "spacing": 4,

    "modules-left": ["clock"],
    "modules-center": ["hyprland/workspaces", "custom/taskbar-divider-edp", "custom/taskbar-divider-hdmi", "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar"],
    "modules-right": ["network", "bluetooth", "battery"],

    "hyprland/workspaces": {
        "format": "{name}",
	"all-outputs": true,
	"ignore-hidden": false,
        "on-click": "activate"
    },

    "custom/taskbar-divider-edp": {
	"exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/workspace-tabs.sh eDP-1",
	"return-type": "json",
	"restart-interval": 0,
	"output": "eDP-1"
    },

    "custom/taskbar-divider-hdmi": {
	"exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/workspace-tabs.sh HDMI-A-1",
	"return-type": "json",
	"restart-interval": 0,
	"output": "HDMI-A-1"
    },

    "hyprland/workspaces#taskbar": {
	"format": "{windows}",
	"all-outputs": false,
	"active-only": true,
	"on-click": "activate",
	"workspace-taskbar": {
	    "enable": true,
	    "format": "{icon}",
	    "icon-size": 20,
	    "icon-theme": ["Papirus"],
	    "orientation": "horizontal"
	}
    },

    "clock": {
        "format": "{:%H:%M}",
        "tooltip-format": "{:%A, %B %d, %Y}"
    },

    "network": {
	"interface": "wlo1",
	"format": "{ifname}",
	"format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%)  ",
	"format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"format-disconnected": "", //An empty format will hide the module.
	"format-disconnected": "",
	"tooltip-format": "{ifname}",
	"tooltip-format-wifi": "{essid} ({signalStrength}%) ",
	"tooltip-format-ethernet": "{ifname} ",
	"tooltip-format-disconnected": "Disconnected",
	"max-length": 50
    },

    "battery": {
        "format": "{capacity}% {icon}",
        "format-icons": ["[    ]", "[█   ]", "[██  ]", "[███ ]", "[████]"]
    },

    "bluetooth": {
	"format": " {status}",
	"format-disabled": "", // an empty format will hide the module
	"format-connected": " {num_connections}C",
	"tooltip-format": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}",
	"tooltip-format-connected": "{controller_alias}\t{controller_address}\n\n{device_enumerate}",
	"tooltip-format-enumerate-connected": "{device_alias}\t{device_address}"
    }
}

content.text:
Good — no state changed (the dispatch attempts failed cleanly, no side effects), and waybar is still running fine with the divider working on the non-empty case.

**Summary of this round's changes:**

- **Divider**: replaced the old always-on CSS `border-left` (which persisted even when a workspace was empty) with a tiny live script — repurposed the previously-unused `workspace-tabs.sh` into a `custom/taskbar-divider` module. It reads `hyprctl -j monitors`/`clients`, and emits `│` only if the current output's active workspace has ≥1 window, else an empty string — which waybar auto-hides with zero footprint (same pattern your config already uses for `network`/`bluetooth`'s `format-disconnected: ""`). It auto-detects which monitor it's running on via waybar's `$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME` env var, so one script/module instance correctly serves both eDP-1 and HDMI-A-1 independently — no hardcoded duplication needed (I initially tried two hardcoded per-monitor modules using a bar-level `output` key, which turned out to only apply to whole bars, not individual modules, hence a stray double-divider — fixed by switching to `WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME`).
- **Empty-workspace blob**: added `#workspaces.taskbar button.active { background: transparent; }` so when the active workspace has 0 windows, the taskbar's own highlight box doesn't show a small colored blob — it now blends invisibly into the panel background.

**Verified:**
- Non-empty case, both monitors: single clean divider, icons, no trailing space (screenshots above).
- Empty case: confirmed the divider script's logic directly against workspace 3 (0 clients → outputs `{"text": ""}`), and the taskbar module's empty-collapse CSS was already visually verified earlier. I stopped short of live-switching a monitor to the empty workspace to eyeball it, since your `hyprctl dispatch` is intercepted by some custom Lua wrapper here that rejected the normal syntax (`hl.dispatch(...)` parse error) — I didn't want to poke at that blind on your live session. If you want, switch to workspace 3 on either monitor yourself and let me know if it looks right; happy to adjust further.
